programme.desc: En sammensveiset gjeng med brannmenn i West Virginia får sjokk da de oppdager at en mistenkelig brann viser seg å skjule et trippelmord.

programme.title: Highway To Hell
programme.desc: Et ektepar kjører til Ohio på jakt etter drømmehjemmet. Men etter bare en time får et tilsynelatende tilfeldig overfall tragiske følger.

programme.title: American Monster
programme.desc: Det blir funnet to lik etter en bilulykke, og etterforskerne avdekker den nifse sannheten om et tilsynelatende perfekt parforhold.

programme.title: Disappeared
programme.desc: Etter at Leahs foreldre dør, drar hun på en sjelegranskende reise. Men når bilen hennes blir funnet vraket og forlatt i en nasjonalpark, blir politi og familie forvirret.

programme.title: Disappeared
programme.desc: Når statsadvokat Ray Gricar ikker kommer tilbake fra en kort kjøretur på landet, prøver etterforskerne å finne spor som kan forklare hans forsvinning.

programme.title: I'd Kill for You
programme.desc: Kampen om foreldreretten truer med å ødelegge livene til familien Carpenter. Når datteren, en stjerneadvokat, blir involvert, fører det til sex og bedrageri.

programme.title: I'd Kill for You
programme.desc: Hvor langt vil du gå for den du elsker? Dette programmet tar for seg utrolige forbrytelser hvor kjærlighet eller hengivenhet prioriteres over et menneskes liv.

programme.title: Living A Nightmare
programme.desc: En 23-år gammel mann blir savnet i det lille samfunnet Beech Island i Sør-Carolina. Mens familien leter etter ham, dukker det opp en illevarslende tekstmelding som øker mysteriet.

programme.title: Living A Nightmare
programme.desc: En 20 år gammel student i Ohio blir savnet etter at hun syklet hjem fra kjærestens hus. Etterforskerne begynner en hektisk jakt for å finne henne.

programme.title: Southern Fried Homicide
programme.desc: Politiet finner Genores forslåtte lik etter at hun blir meldt savnet. Men ingen fiender kan finnes, og de forstår ikke hvem som kan ha elsket henne til døde.

programme.desc: Steve og Amy besøker en skrekkslagen kvinne i California som hevder hjemmet hennes angripes av det overnaturlige. Hun tror en ånd drepte romkameraten.

programme.title: Historier fra Zambia
programme.desc: Trærne er Afrikas eldste beboere, og hver av dem har sin egen strategi for å overleve tørketiden. Pølsetreet og fikentreet holder ut årstidenes ekstreme forhold for å gi dyrene mat og ly i magre tider. Til gjengjeld hjelper dyrene disse trærne med å formere seg ved å bestøve blomstene deres og spre frøene. Afrikanske trær fremmer liv og er ryggraden i et av de mest verdifulle økosystemene i verden.

programme.title: Planet Merkelig
programme.desc: Gå inn i ringen med naturens største slåsskjemper, som bruker vold for å få det de trenger. Se kannibaledderkoppen spise opp motstanderen, se den blodtørstige siden av koselige koalaer og få med deg en nakkeslengende giraffkamp.

programme.title: Planet Merkelig
programme.desc: Bli med på innsiden av de tøffeste gjengene i verden, og se hva pågangsmot er i naturen. Følg en flokk plyndrende gresshopper, se kokosnøttblekkspruten gå i bakholdsangrep og møt en flokk med finker som har fått smaken på blod.

programme.title: Hakkespetter – hele historien
programme.desc: Marsjer til den taktfaste trommelyden av en unik fuglefamilie. Finn ut hvorfor verdens 239 store og små hakkespettarter er naturens beste tømmerhuggere. Se hvordan de flyr, klatrer og kaller på hverandre, og få et innblikk i de hemmelige redene deres.

programme.title: Min beste venn er et dyr
programme.desc: Sjekk at dovendyret Elsa har det bra med Pedro, som har viet livet sitt til å ta vare på henne etter at hun ble lam. Få vite hvorfor ulven Thor har mennesket Steve i flokken, og se Kristen og Beau gjøre livet enklere for vaskebjørnen Crystal.

programme.title: Min beste venn er et dyr
programme.desc: Lær å svømme med oteren Ozzy og treneren Leslie, og se hvordan Petronel har fått det foreldreløse neshornet Riris tillit etter å ha blitt traumatisert av krypskyttere. Snus deg frem til landminer med rotta Kobe, og fridykk med hammerhaien Gaia.

programme.title: Kampen om herredømme
programme.desc: I Australia finner vi en rekke forskjellige skapninger, og like mange måter å lykkes på som alfahann eller - hunn. Stranden blir til en duellplass og villmarken blir til en boksering når dyrene slåss seg imellom.

programme.title: Min beste venn er et dyr

programme.title: Afrikas jegere
programme.desc: Et banebrytende varmekamera avslører den hemmelige tilværelsen til nattaktive rovdyr. Følg med når en av de eldste leopardene vi kjenner til, kjemper for å klare seg mot de fryktinnjagende naboene sine: en flokk løver på jakt etter mat.

programme.title: Månens ville side
programme.desc: Dra ut på episke reiser styrt av månens kraft. Se hvordan usynlige signaler styrer hvaler og skilpadders migrasjonsruter i havet, fly på tvers av kontinenter med nattravner, og se kompostbiller og andre insekter navigere ved hjelp av måneskinnet.

programme.title: Kimberley - Australias ville vestkyst
programme.desc: Unngå skjelldekte og fjærkledde farer med wallabyer, se krageagamer kjempe om maker, og bli med på etegilde med nyklekkede krokodiller. Utforsk farlige stryk og forstår den kulturelle og biologiske viktigheten av en lokal elv i regnsesongen.

programme.title: Røtter

programme.desc: Få et innblikk i verdens største biomassevandring, den årlige, 1600 kilometer lange sardinvandringen langs østkysten av Sør-Afrika. Se milliarder av disse bittesmå fiskene svømme slalåm mellom sultne rovdyr som listige seler og stupende havsuler.

programme.title: Kampen om herredømme
programme.desc: Savannen i Afrika er et fantastisk landskap, og uansett om det dreier seg om stangende flodhester, hormonelle elefanter eller duellerende løver, er slagene som utspiller seg på savannen, like fantastiske.

programme.title: Kenyas villmarkshistorier
programme.desc: Lewa Conservancy arbeider for å føre elefanter tilbake til området fra Mt. Kenya til Samburu nasjonalpark. De har også opprettet en avsperret sone for elefanter for å forsøke å gjenoppbygge et skadet økosystem. Sporingshalsbånd brukes i begge tilfeller for å hjelpe naturvernerne med å forstå elefantens behov bedre, og for å se om de vender tilbake til de naturlige korridorene.

programme.title: Ukjente landskap
programme.desc: Lær om verdens største vulkanske øy, et ensomt og forrevent sted der damp slippes ut, vann eksploderer og nytt terreng dannes hver dag. Se hvordan ild og is møtes i et slag som gjør dette til den mest geologisk kraftfulle øya i verden.

programme.title: Ukjente landskap
programme.desc: Bli med på en reise på en øy bygget av vulkaner, men formet av is. For ca. 1,5 millioner år siden kom et islag nordfra og la seg over landskapet. I dag fortsetter enorme isbreer å skjære ut klipper og file ned fjell.

programme.title: Ukjente landskap
programme.desc: Bli med til det brusende havet i Fundybukta og finn ut hvordan dette økosystemet på østkysten av Canada livnærer en rekke skapninger, deriblant hundretusenvis av sjøfugler, verdens raskeste rovdyr og et innviklet nett av virvelløse dyr.

programme.title: Ukjente landskap
programme.desc: Bli med langs vestkysten av Storbritannia, der verdens lengste ubrutte gangsti strekker seg gjennom over 1200 kilometer med storslått landskap. Denne majestetiske kysten yrer av ville dyr, geologiske mysterier og mange hundre år med menneskenes historie.

programme.title: Ukjente landskap
programme.desc: Bli kjent med en øy som er omgitt av det mektige Atlanterhavet, prisgitt knusende bølger og kraftig regn. Fra Cliffs of Moher til Giant's Causeway har dette landet blitt formet og omformet av vann og voldsomme geologiske krefter.

programme.title: Ukjente landskap
programme.desc: Bli med til den ville stillehavskysten på vestsiden av Vancouver Island i British Columbia. Naturen og menneskene eksisterer side ved side i spektakulære habitater, fra isbreer i fjellene til tretoppene i Canadas eneste regnskog.

programme.title: Røtter
programme.desc: På tvers av bølgete sanddyner, i de vindblåste gressområdene i den sørlige Kalahari tårner et praktfullt kameltre. Den har stått her i to århundrer. Dette treet er aldri ensomt, lær hvordan det gir mat, ly og et jaktterreng til mange skapninger.

programme.title: Røtter
programme.desc: Oppdag historien om det høyt elskede pølsetreet, hvis nektarfylte blomster og pølseformede frukter lokker dyr av alle slag, fra insekter til elefanter. Se hvordan dyrene som stoler på dette sjenerøse treet sikrer spredningen.

programme.title: Røtter
programme.desc: I en tåkete sørafrikansk skog vokser et seks hundre år gammelt Outeniqua tre. Med sine førti meter ruver hun høyt over over kalesjen og er en av de få som er igjen av sitt slag. Følg hennes fengslende historie, like unik som økosystemet i grenene hennes.

programme.title: Røtter
programme.desc: Namaqua-bergfikentreet lever i skråningen på en steinete høyde i Manaqualand i Sør-Afrika. Det er den ultimate overlevende som tåler de ugjestmilde forholdene i et landskap som hvert år opplever stadig stigende temperaturer og mindre og mindre regn.

programme.title: Sjefshai
programme.desc: Se den ultimate kampen for dominans mens vitenskapsmenn prøver å identifisere alfahannen i en flokk på over 100 hvithaier ved kysten av New Zealand. Bli imponert av hastigheten, jaktferdighetene og fryktløsheten som avgjør hvem som skal lede flokken.

programme.title: Superhaienes hovedvei
programme.desc: Dra ut på et farlig merkingsoppdrag i Sør-Australia som viser hva haier spiser og hvorfor de samles på matplasser. Sett så kursen nordover når teamet prøver å finner tiger-, okse- og hammerhaier og utstyrer en av dem med et 360-graders ryggkamera.

programme.title: Superhaienes hovedvei
programme.desc: Følg en gravid hai langs Great Barrier Reef og se om hun bringer forskningsteamet til sin hemmelige fødeplass. Se etter tegn på parring langs sørkysten, som kan avsløre en veldig sjenert megahai-hunn på jakt etter en partner.

programme.title: Superhaienes hovedvei
programme.desc: Vær våken til langt på natt når teamet i nord fester en aktivitetsmåler på en oksehai og finner ut hva denne nattugla gjør etter solnedgang. Dykk ned til 80 meter med teamet i sør, som håper å feste en satellitt-tracker på en hvithai-hunn.

programme.title: Superhaienes hovedvei
programme.desc: La deg forundre av hierarkiet i haisamfunn når det nordre teamet ser på unge svartstripehaier som lærer sosiale regler og overlevelse. Ved Rainbow Beach er det sørlige teamet ivrige på å bevitne sandtigerhaien best skjulte adferd: parring.

programme.title: Superhaienes hovedvei
programme.desc: Reis til enden av Australias haimotorvei. Finn ut om Greenly Island i sør er en rasteplass for migrerende hvithaier, og se etter bevis på en genetisk sammenheng mellom nordlige oksehaier og deres søskenbarn i kjøligere områder.

programme.title: Superhaienes hovedvei
programme.sub-title: Forsiktig, det er mennesker der oppe!
programme.desc: Følg det sørlige teamet når de tester ny migrasjonsteknologi og verktøy som kan redusere haiangrep i et populært snorkleområde. Bli med på å fange og merke oksehaier med det nordlige teamet, som vil hjelpe svømmere med å unngå fødende mødre.

programme.title: Superhaienes hovedvei

programme.title: Superhaienes hovedvei

programme.title: Hollywood Gala
programme.desc: Swiss conductor Ludwig Wicki leads the Danish National Symphony Orchestra and the DR Junior Choir in a sparkling concert program of film music. The program features a selection of music from great and Oscar-winning Hollywood films, including Titanic, The Bodyguard, Pirates of the Caribbean, Braveheart, and Moulin Rouge, written by major composers such as John Williams, Hans Zimmer, James Horner, and Klaus Badelt. Highlights include ‘He’s a pirate/Davy Jones’ from Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man’s Chest; ‘Now We Are Free’ from Gladiator; ‘My Heart Will Go On’ from Titanic; and ‘Shallow’ from A Star Is Born. Featured soloists in this concert are the young talented singers Andrea Lykke Oehlenschlæger and Diluckshan Jeyaratnam. This performance was recorded at the DR Koncerthuset in Copenhagen, Denmark, in May 2022.

programme.title: Electronic Vibrations - A sound changes the world
programme.desc: Whether techno or hip-hop – electronic music is nowadays the driving force of pop culture. We have almost forgotten that its origins lie in the WDR’s electronic studio, which made Cologne to one of the centres of the avant-garde during the post-war years. This is the story of how a room full of strange devices would become a cabinet of curiosities, the vibrations of which sent the whole world in a state of ecstasy. From the beginnings directly after the Second World War in Paris with Pierre Schaeffer’s ‘musique concrète’, the film focuses on Stockhausen and goes on to Kraftwerk, from Jean-Michel Jarre and the IRCAM studio right up to Detroit to the beginnings of techno.Subtitles available for this program with your remote control.

programme.title: Architectures
programme.desc: In 1050, one of the first major pilgrimage churches in the Western world was built at Conques, in the middle of the wild Aveyron landscape. This was the birth of "Romanesque" architecture. The abbey church - i.e., a church belonging to an abbey - at Conques is one of the most important structures built in 11th-century France. Its coherence, its location - a small village in the Rouergue region, far from the main medieval traffic routes - its innovative aspect, its state of preservation and the fact that the relics for which it was built are still in situ, make the church at Conques the best work of art for approaching Romanesque architecture in France. In other words, to try and understand how architecture was made at that time in our history, and to dismantle not only the building itself, but also a number of preconceived ideas about Romanesque art, starting with its very name, which is an intellectual construct of the 19th century, or to put it another way: those who built Conques.

programme.title: Artist's Workshop
programme.desc: Dans cet épisode, nous nous intéresserons à l’artiste Robert Combas. Sa peinture est faite de libertés : elle parle de la société, de la violence, de la sexualité, de la souffrance des gens, de leurs petits bonheurs, de leur petitesse, de leur grandeur… Il s’inspire du rock dont il est un fin amateur, des images populaires des livres d’enfance, des manuels scolaires, et de tout ce qui fait une culture populaire accessible à tous.

programme.title: Artist's Workshop
programme.desc: François Boucq draws from morning to night in his studio, alone, as if he wanted to be more closely involved with his characters, moving from the savagery of the American West to the diplomacy of the Vatican, from the urban jungle to the news of the daily press. He has been drawing for 40 years with realism, with a precise and detailed line, a graphic finesse that makes him one of the undisputed masters of today's comics.

programme.title: Exhibition on Screen
programme.desc: With loans from across the world, this major retrospective brings together Vermeer’s most famous masterpieces including Girl with a Pearl Earring, The Geographer, The Milkmaid, The Little Street, Lady Writing a Letter with her Maid, and Woman Holding a Balance. In all, 28 of his surviving 37 works. This film invites audiences to a privileged view of the exhibition, accompanied by the director of the Rijksmuseum and the curators of the show. A truly once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to discover the genius of Vermeer and his fascinating and mysterious life.

programme.title: Within The Frame
programme.desc: Leader of the School of Pont-Aven, Paul Gauguin, the most exotic of French artists, paved the way for modern painting. There were two main themes which marked his work: Brittany and Tahiti. A rebel, he rejected copying reality in favour of exploring more delicate painting techniques. You will discover here the most important milestones in his work: from “Four Breton Girls” to “Tahitian Women on the Beach”, by way of the surprising “Self Portrait with Yellow Christ”. Enjoy your visit!

programme.title: Within The Frame
programme.desc: Léonard De Vinci est le peintre Italien de la renaissance le plus célèbre. Il possède un talent inégalable (peintre, sculpteur, architecte, ingénieur, urbaniste, mathématicien, botaniste, philosophe, inventeur,…) Il a considérablement influencé l’histoire de l’art. Son usage de la technique Sfumato et du clair-obscur son encore étudié aujourd’hui. La « Mona Lisa » et « La Cène » exposé au Louvre et dans l'église Santa Maria delle Grazie qui apparaissent dans cet épisode font partie de ses peintures les plus renommé, admiré et parodié à travers le monde.Bonne visite !

programme.title: Sketchbook
programme.desc: Raphael Federici (street artist), Marine Goodmorning (illustrator), Luca Fiore (cartoonist) and Harry Boudchicha (drawing teacher) reveal their best drawing techniques. Each episode focuses on a specific subject:movement, oil painting, shadows, hair... For the first 10 minutes, each artist gives a theoretical lesson illustrated by sketches. Then they each start working on their creation. Finally, they end with a debrief, comparingand explaining their techniques.

programme.title: Little Sketches
programme.desc: In 64 episodes, fun and educational, you will know how to draw an airplane, a fireman, a haunted mansion, a soccer player, a sunset, a lion, the Eiffel Tower, seashells, a fairy... Our master draftsman Gia-Haï Phan will show you the basics of a successful drawing: proportions, perspectives, values, contrasts, volumes, blending, everything is covered.

programme.title: Architectures
programme.desc: The Van Eetvelde Hotel, a three-story private house, built between 1895 and 1897, in Brussels, Avenue Palmerston. The man who had it built: Edmond Van Eetvelde, a senior civil servant whose career is on the rise. To build his house, Van Eetvelde chose Victor Horta, a young avant-garde architect, one of the founders of the Art Nouveau movement.

programme.title: Exhibition on Screen
programme.desc: The Impressionists are the most popular group in art history - millions flock every year to marvel at their masterpieces. But, to begin with, they were scorned, penniless outsiders. 1874 was the year that changed everything; the first Impressionists, “hungry for independence”, broke the mould by holding their own exhibition outside official channels. Impressionism was born and the art world was changed forever.What led to that first groundbreaking show 150 years ago? Who were the maverick personalities that wielded their brushes in such a radical and provocative way? The spectacular Musée d’Orsay exhibition brings fresh eyes to this extraordinary tale of passion and rebellion. The story is told not by historians and curators but in the words of those who witnessed the dawn of Impressionism: the artists, press and people of Paris, 1874. See the show that changed everything on the big screen.

programme.title: Exhibition on Screen
programme.desc: En juin 2017, une grande exposition a ouvert à Paris au musée d’Orsay. Pour la première fois, cette exposition a réuni tous les portraits de Cézanne. Cela a été l’occasion d’analyser l’œuvre de Cézanne à l’aide d’experts internationaux et de parcourir les salles de la National Portrait Gallery de Londres et de la National Gallery of Art de Washington.

programme.title: Exhibition on Screen
programme.desc: Hopper’s work is the most recognisable art in America – popular, praised, and mysterious. Countless painters, photographers, filmmakers and musicians have been influenced by his art – but who was he, and how did a struggling illustrator create such a bounty of notable work?This new film takes a deep look into Hopper’s art, his life, and his relationships. From his early career as an illustrator; his wife giving up her own promising art career to be his manager; his critical and commercial acclaim; and in his own words – this film explores the enigmatic personality behind the brush….

programme.title: Within The Frame
programme.desc: L’art d’Edgar Degas est difficile à classer, cependant il est souvent associé au mouvement impressionniste, qui a émergé en France à la fin du 19ème siècle. Néanmoins, il a développé un style très personnel avec une préférence pour les sujets intérieurs plutôt que les scènes en plein air favorisées par les peintres impressionnistes. Les 10 oeuvres présentées dans cet épisode illustrent parfaitement les préférences thématiques d’Edgar Degas : Le spectacle, le bain, les portraits de famille et les classes de travail. Découvrez " La Classe de danse " exposé au Musée d'Orsay ou encore " Les Danseuses bleues " au Musée des Beaux-Arts Pouchkine.Bonne visite !

programme.title: Within The Frame
programme.desc: Discover or re-discover the masterpieces of the greatest painters of history through our documentary series Within The Frame. From impressionists to surrealists, from Leonard Da Vinci to Paul Cézanne, every episode will immerge you into a virtual tour of a paintings collection. You will see the most impressive paintings ever made and won't miss a single detail.

programme.title: My little Museum
programme.desc: My little Museum is Art History retold through funny anecdotes and backstage trivias by Alicia Flipo. With her wacky demeanor, her inventiveness and her quirky sense of humor, Alicia stages these small Art tales so that once and for all, you could remember the Big stories!

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Two favourite Blue Peter presenters Sarah Greene and Peter Duncan are in the company of Natasha Raskin and Catherine Southon as they hunt for antiques around Surrey, Hertfordshire and North West London. Peter detours to learn how hockey became a popular sport the world over while keen aviator Sarah sees how the Battle of Britain was won. An incredible haul of antiques, including chimney pots, Pinocchio and a pair of African fertility figures, go under the gavel at an auction in Tewkesbury, Gloucestershire.

programme.title: Exhibition on Screen
programme.desc: 200 years after it opened and a century after acquiring its first Van Gogh works, the National Gallery hosted the largest Van Gogh exhibition ever held in the UK (September 14, 2024 to January 19, 2025). The exhibition was a huge success, unanimously praised by the press, and tickets sold out quickly, making this film the only way to see what Forbes called a “once-in-a-lifetime exhibition.”Discover the passion that drove one of the world's most beloved artists to revolutionize art. Van Gogh: Poets & Lovers rewrites history and celebrates Van Gogh's genius without exploiting his suffering, allowing audiences to truly understand this iconic artist in a whole new way...

programme.title: Exhibition on Screen
programme.desc: The Kiss by Gustav Klimt is one of the most recognised and reproduced paintings in the world. It is perhaps the most popular poster on student dorm walls from Beijing to Boston. Painted in Vienna around 1908, the evocative image of an unknown embracing couple has captivated viewers with its mystery, sensuality and dazzling materials ever since it was created. But just what lies behind the appeal of the painting – and just who was the artist that created it? Delving into the details of real gold, decorative designs, symbolism and simmering erotica, a close study of the painting takes us to the remarkable turn of the century Vienna when a new world was battling with the old.

programme.title: Private Tour
programme.desc: Private Tour takes you to discover the exhibition "Architects furniture, 1960-2020" at the Cité de l'Architecture et du Patrimoine in Paris. Why do architects still design furniture today, while designers have taken over the real estate market, lighting...? You will have the answer in this private tour and you will discover furniture of architects such as Nemo.

programme.title: Exhibition on Screen
programme.desc: This eagerly-awaited exhibition at the Royal Academy of Arts was the first-ever retrospective devoted to the portraiture of Édouard Manet. Covering the entire career of this enigmatic and sometimes controversial artist, the exhibition brought together works from Europe, Asia and the United States. Manet's portraiture has never been the subject of an exhibition, although it represents around half of his artistic output. He painted his family, friends and the literary, political and artistic figures of the day, bringing to life not only his subjects but also Parisian society.

programme.title: Exhibition on Screen
programme.sub-title: Le collectionneur danois : de Delacroix à Gauguin
programme.desc: Wilhelm Hansen fut un homme d’affaires visionnaire, qui vécut au Danemark au XIXème siècle. Il fut l’un des rares collectionneurs à s’intéresser aux peintres impressionnistes, à une époque où ils étaient attaqués et dénigrés. Le film nous amène dans la maison d’été de Hansen dans la banlieue de Copenhague et nous fait visiter l’extraordinaire exposition à la Royal Academy de Londres consacrée à sa collection.

programme.title: Graffiti World
programme.desc: Graffiti World is a short program dedicated to contemporary urban art around the world. Each episode explores a specific city, highlighting iconic works of street art. Local soundscape accompanies the images for an authentic, commentary-free immersion. The program showcases the creativity and diversity of artistic expression in public spaces. An invitation to discover the richness of graffiti as an art form in its own right.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Legends of stage and screen, Charles Dance and Geraldine James join antiques experts Natasha Raskin and Will Axon on this Road Trip romp around Wiltshire. Charles finds a pair of Edwardian silver vases he hopes will prove profitable at an auction in Essex. Geraldine, however, bumps into a chap in the street with a 19th Century French Empire secretaire. It costs her a small fortune – will the gamble pay off? A diversion from the shops sees Charles end up in the cockpit of a very old helicopter while Geraldine learns how a small part of Swindon dating back 170 years influenced the creation of the modern NHS.

programme.title: Exhibition on Screen
programme.desc: Based on a major exhibition at the Ashmolean Museum in Oxford, Tokyo Stories spans 400 years of incredibly rich art, from Hokusai’s prints to Pop Art posters, via contemporary photography, manga, cinema and street art. The exhibition was a huge success and attracted a significantly younger and more diverse audience than usual. The film draws on the exhibition to take us to Tokyo and explore the city’s art and artistic figures in greater depth. A superbly illustrated and richly detailed documentary, which traces the journey of a metropolis marked by ceaseless cycles of destruction and rebirth throughout its 400-year history, to become one of the most dynamic and fascinating cities in the world today.

programme.title: Architectures
programme.sub-title: Charlety, a stadium in the city
programme.desc: Découvrez un bâtiment de l’architecture classique, moderne ou contemporaine avec une « leçons d’architecture » conjuguant rigueur, plaisir et intelligence. Au stade Charlety, les architectes ont réussi à concilier les contraires : la grandeur monumentale du stade avec celle du quartier, la vie d’une cité sportive avec celle des bureaux. Situé à la porte de Gentilly à Paris, coincé entre le périphérique et le boulevard des Maréchaux, le stade Charléty est bordé des pavillons de la Cité universitaire, d’un cimetière et de HLM en briques rouges. Sur ce site difficile de huit hectares, marqué par les cinquante ans d’histoire de l’ancien stade Sébastien-Charléty, Henri Gaudin et son fils Bruno ont su implanter le volume massif d’un stade de 20 000 places couvertes, ainsi que les équipements sportifs et les bureaux commandés par la Ville de Paris. En concevant ce grand stade avec sa forme d’anneau gigantesque, ses gradins en ellipse et sa toiture aérienne, les architectes ont su traduire l’é.

programme.title: Architectures
programme.desc: Located near Compiègne, Château de Pierrefonds was one of Jean de Berry's most powerful châteaux, dismantled and gutted by order of Richelieu in the 17th century, and one of the most beautiful medieval ruins to inspire so much romantic nostalgia in the 19th century. A ruin bought by Napoleon III, who wished to transform it into an imperial residence...

programme.title: Stolen Treasures
programme.sub-title: The 5 Masterpieces of the Museum of Modern Art – Paris
programme.desc: In 2010, five masterpieces by Picasso, Matisse, Braque, Modigliani and Léger went missing. A year into the investigation, the police arrested the burglar, Vrejan Tomic. A repeat offender, with 11 art thefts to his name, he usually works to order. In this case, the client was Jean-Michel Corvez. Wrapped in bin bags, these unsellable works were found at the home of a third man, Yonathan Birn. How? Why?

programme.title: Stolen Treasures
programme.desc: Painted by the Van Eyck brothers, ‘The Adoration of the Mystical Lamb’ or ‘The Ghent Altarpiece’ is regarded as one of the greatest masterpieces of the Flemish Primitives. Installed in St Bavon’s Cathedral in Ghent as early as 1432, it escaped theft and looting on several occasions, However, on the night of 10–11 April 1934, two panels were stolen, one of which – ‘The Just Judges’ – has never been recovered to this day, because the bishop refused to pay the ransom demanded….

programme.title: Stolen Treasures
programme.desc: On the night of 17–18 October 1984, three criminals broke into the municipal museum in Semur-en-Auxois, which was not fitted with an alarm system. The joint investigation by the French and Japanese police revealed links between the Parisian underworld and the Japanese Yakuza mafia. Indeed, Shinchi Fujikuma, a Japanese gangster, had met two members of the Aubervilliers gang, Philippe-Emile Jamin and Youssef Khimoun, whilst serving time in a French prison. In 1987, the French managed to return from Japan with four of the five stolen paintings. The last one, *The Portrait of Mrs Baudot*, remained with its new owner, in accordance with the principle of ‘good faith’ guaranteed by Japanese law.

programme.title: Stolen Treasures
programme.sub-title: Looting of the Gentili Di Giuseppe Collection
programme.desc: Federico Gentili di Giuseppe was a Jewish businessman of Italian origin with a passion for art. On his death in 1940, he bequeathed a collection of 150 paintings to his two children, Marcel and Adriana, who had become naturalised French citizens. In 1941, Maître Moulin auctioned off these paintings under questionable circumstances. This marked the beginning of a legal battle waged by the Gentili di Giuseppe heirs, which was to last nearly 50 years.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Comedy legend Jennifer Saunders and best pal, top actress Patricia Potter take to the road on a humdinger of a trip. Joined by veteran antiquers Phillip Serrell and Mark Stacey they shop in Berkshire, Hampshire and Oxfordshire before heading for an auction in Greenwich, London. Jennifer and Phil detour to hear about Fred Karno, the man credited with inventing slapstick comedy. While Patricia and Mark learn how a surgeon from Reading used his incredible sense of smell to successfully treat soldiers injured in World War One.And, Phil gets custard pied – what’s not to love?

programme.title: Exhibition on Screen
programme.sub-title: Degas : une passion de la perfection
programme.desc: Exhibition on screen nous emmène à travers les rues de Paris puis au cœur d’une superbe exposition au Fitzwilliam Museum de Cambridge, dont l’impressionnante collection d’œuvres de Degas est la plus représentative de Grande-Bretagne. Ayant bénéficié d’un accès exclusif à une grande variété d’œuvres rares, le film raconte l’histoire fascinante de la quête de perfection de Degas à travers l’expérimentation de nouvelles techniques et les leçons apprises en étudiant les grands maîtres.

programme.title: Exhibition on Screen
programme.desc: With loans from across the world, this major retrospective brings together Vermeer’s most famous masterpieces including Girl with a Pearl Earring, The Geographer, The Milkmaid, The Little Street, Lady Writing a Letter with her Maid, and Woman Holding a Balance. In all, 28 of his surviving 37 works. This film invites audiences to a privileged view of the exhibition, accompanied by the director of the Rijksmuseum and the curators of the show. A truly once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to discover the genius of Vermeer and his fascinating and mysterious life.

programme.title: Exhibition on Screen
programme.desc: In 2013, Norway celebrated the 150th anniversary of the birth of Edvard Munch (1863-1944), one of the most prominent figures in modern art. Munch 150, co-produced by the National Museum and the Munch Museum, is already being hailed as "the exhibition of a lifetime". Public interest is enormous, as evidenced by the record-breaking $120 million public auction result for one of his four paintings, The Scream. This presentation will take you behind the scenes of how this exhibition came to be, as well as including a guided tour of Norway, outlining the biography of this man whose life spanned the mid-19th century to the German occupation during the Second World War.

programme.title: Exhibition on Screen
programme.desc: Without Camille Pissarro, there is no Impressionist movement. He is rightfully known as the father of Impressionism.It was a dramatic path that Pissarro followed, and throughout it all he wrote extensively to his family. It is through these intimate and revealing letters that this gripping film reveals Pissarro’s life and work.Born in the West Indies, Pissarro found his passion in paint as a young man in Paris, and by the age of 43 had corralled a group of enthusiastic artists into a new collective. Their first show was scorned by the critics, but the group had acquired a new name: the Impressionists. For the next 40 years Pissarro was the driving force behind what has today become the world’s favourite artistic movement.The Ashmolean Museum has a long tradition of excellence. As the UK’s first ever public museum (it opened its doors in May 1683) it houses a wonderfully rich collection, including the remarkable Pissarro archive. With exclusive access to most extensive archive of.

programme.title: Graffiti World
programme.desc: Graffiti World is a short program dedicated to contemporary urban art around the world. Each episode explores a specific city, highlighting iconic works of street art. Local soundscape accompanies the images for an authentic, commentary-free immersion. The program showcases the creativity and diversity of artistic expression in public spaces. An invitation to discover the richness of graffiti as an art form in its own right.

programme.title: Exhibition on Screen
programme.sub-title: John Singer Sargent: Fashion and Swagger
programme.desc: John Singer Sargent is known as the greatest portrait artist of his era. What made his ‘swagger’ portraits remarkable was his power over his sitters, what they wore and how they were presented to the audience. Through interviews with curators, contemporary fashionistas and style influencers, Exhibition on Screen’s film will examine how Sargent’s unique practice has influenced modern art, culture and fashion.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Two luvvies from the world of stage and TV, Ruth Madoc and Su Pollard, best known for their appearances in sitcom Hi-De-Hi, are antique hunting with Phil Serrell and Raj Bisram. Setting off from the Welsh border town of Monmouth they head for auction in Congleton, Cheshire. Ruth also gets to find out about the incredible 19th century nurse – and it’s not Florence Nightingale – whilst Su visits ancient Roman town Caerleon and finds time for an amphitheatre showdown with Phil. And Su attempts to resolve an age old mystery...does Phil wear a wig?

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Two stars of the seventies, cool crooner Tony Christie and pop royalty Jimmy Osmond are accompanied by experts Catherine Southon and Margie Cooper. Blasting off from the Leicestershire town of Loughborough they’ll head for an auction in the Staffordshire city of Stoke-on-Trent. Tony squeezes in a visit to Coalbrookdale, the place where ground breaking techniques were developed that kick-started the industrial revolution. And petrol-head Jimmy gets to whizz round the historical race circuit at Donington. The big auction finale includes a sing-a-long like no other. But which musical maestro will clinch victory?

programme.title: Stolen Treasures
programme.desc: On the night of 17–18 October 1984, three criminals broke into the municipal museum in Semur-en-Auxois, which was not fitted with an alarm system. The joint investigation by the French and Japanese police revealed links between the Parisian underworld and the Japanese Yakuza mafia. Indeed, Shinchi Fujikuma, a Japanese gangster, had met two members of the Aubervilliers gang, Philippe-Emile Jamin and Youssef Khimoun, whilst serving time in a French prison. In 1987, the French managed to return from Japan with four of the five stolen paintings. The last one, *The Portrait of Mrs Baudot*, remained with its new owner, in accordance with the principle of ‘good faith’ guaranteed by Japanese law.

programme.title: Stolen Treasures
programme.desc: Painted by the Van Eyck brothers, ‘The Adoration of the Mystical Lamb’ or ‘The Ghent Altarpiece’ is regarded as one of the greatest masterpieces of the Flemish Primitives. Installed in St Bavon’s Cathedral in Ghent as early as 1432, it escaped theft and looting on several occasions, However, on the night of 10–11 April 1934, two panels were stolen, one of which – ‘The Just Judges’ – has never been recovered to this day, because the bishop refused to pay the ransom demanded….

programme.title: Stolen Treasures
programme.sub-title: The 5 Masterpieces of the Museum of Modern Art – Paris
programme.desc: In 2010, five masterpieces by Picasso, Matisse, Braque, Modigliani and Léger went missing. A year into the investigation, the police arrested the burglar, Vrejan Tomic. A repeat offender, with 11 art thefts to his name, he usually works to order. In this case, the client was Jean-Michel Corvez. Wrapped in bin bags, these unsellable works were found at the home of a third man, Yonathan Birn. How? Why?

programme.title: Stolen Treasures
programme.desc: Painted in 1911, Pablo Picasso’s "La Coiffeuse" is an iconic work of Cubism. The painting was last seen in 1998, following a loan for an exhibition in Munich. On its return to Paris, it was stored in the Centre Pompidou’s storerooms… until the day it was discovered to be missing, in 2001. Had it been stolen from the storerooms? Sixteen years after the theft, in 2014, a ship docked at the port of Newark, in New Jersey, USA. The artwork was on board….

programme.title: Within The Frame
programme.desc: Claude Monet is probably the best-known painter of the impressionist movement. Indeed, the term “impressionism” was derived from his painting “Impression Rising Sun” (1872). This exhibition retraces the great stages in Monet’s prolific career while dwelling on paintings of this master that cannot be ignored: the “Saint Lazare Station”, the “Poppies near Argenteuil”, the “Haystacks” and the “Rouen Cathedral” exposed all around the world in different museum such as the Museum of Fine Arts in Boston without forgetting his “Water-lilies” exposed at the Orangerie museum in Paris. Enjoy your visit!

programme.title: Within The Frame
programme.desc: Discover or re-discover the masterpieces of the greatest painters of history through our documentary series Within The Frame. From impressionists to surrealists, from Leonard Da Vinci to Paul Cézanne, every episode will immerge you into a virtual tour of a paintings collection. You will see the most impressive paintings ever made and won't miss a single detail.

programme.title: Architectures
programme.desc: Entre 1928 et 1932, le décorateur Pierre Chareau construit à Paris une maison d'avant-garde faite d'acier et de verre. C'est une machine à habiter, poétique et ludique, pleine de surprises et de trouvailles, une œuvre aussi rythmique qu'inclassable.

programme.title: Artist's Workshop
programme.desc: In the Artist's workshop series, we offer you a privileged meeting with an artist, or the discovery of an artist or an important place for the history of art. Whether they are painters, visual artists, sculptors... These people all have the same passion for art and this series is an opportunity to enter their different universes, to discover what drives them, inspires them and maybe that will give rise to vocations.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Two favourite Blue Peter presenters Sarah Greene and Peter Duncan are in the company of Natasha Raskin and Catherine Southon as they hunt for antiques around Surrey, Hertfordshire and North West London. Peter detours to learn how hockey became a popular sport the world over while keen aviator Sarah sees how the Battle of Britain was won. An incredible haul of antiques, including chimney pots, Pinocchio and a pair of African fertility figures, go under the gavel at an auction in Tewkesbury, Gloucestershire.

programme.title: Photo Contest
programme.desc: In each episode of Photo Contest, two contestants compete on an imposed theme such as rock'n roll, Japan or architecture. They have one hour to take the best possible photographs before editing them for 30 minutes in a studio. The photographs they have selected are then presented to Agnès Grégoire, editor-in-chief of PHOTO magazine, who will have to choose the best photographer.

programme.title: Deco Masters
programme.desc: Après quatre jours de compétition acharnée, c'est enfin le jour de la finale. Mais avant de découvrir les notes de leurs propriétaires respectifs, chaque candidat aura l'occasion de savoir ce que pensent ses adversaires de ses choix déco. Et c'est Mickael qui ouvre le bal et qui rejoint notre experte en déco Valérie Damidot. Il est temps pour lui de découvrir si ses camarades ont été aussi stratèges que lui.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: We will start this journey near La Rochelle to learn a little more about the breeding of the famous bouchot mussels but also a very particular technique to cook them. We will then go on a tour of France's best oysters: towards Cancale, Arcachon, Montpellier and finally Oléron to learn about the different breeding methods and to find out more about all the species in France. Julie will cook a fricassee of berniques, the little Chinese hats that cover the rocks of the coast, as well as pink clams that are little known to the public. We will continue our journey in Finistère to meet Sylvain, the only abalone breeder in the country, and then to Méru where there are still workshops magnifying this sublime material. The Chef Jean-Marie Baudic will cook scallops like no one else.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: Julie heads for Burgundy to discover ancient breeds of poultry reintroduced to France thanks to the work of breeder Fred Ménager. We'll then move on to Auvergne to discover how the famous Label Rouge is awarded and the role of certifying bodies ... because it's important to know what ends up on our plates. Julie also travels to the Drôme to cook guinea fowl, before heading to the Périgord to prepare a turkey stew. Julie will then head back up towards the center to discover an amazing fly maker who uses rooster feathers!

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: Eating flowers might appear unconventional, but we often consume them without even realizing it. Consider artichokes, for instance : they are essentially large, unopened flowers. Capers are the preserved buds of flowers soaked in vinegar, and cloves are dried flower buds. We also find courgette flowers, saffron pistils, orange blossom water used to flavor pastries, and the violet sweets that evoke memories of our childhood. In addition to adding aesthetic appeal and providing a dose of vitamins to our plates, flowers elevate the flavors of a dish and can even serve as a vegetable substitute.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: Today, Julie takes us on a tour of spices and aromatic plants. Spices are a call to travel, to faraway lands and to the unknown. In the kitchen, they bear witness to our relationship with others, reflecting our vision of the world. Julie's journey will introduce us to the famous black pepper, thanks to Erwann de Kerros, an insatiable pepper seeker. Aromatic plants will also be in the spotlight, as we pick them with Edouard Loubet in the Luberon...

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: It is in the heart of the Sarthe that Julie begins her new tour. Located in the Pays de la Loire region, the Sarthe department is the gateway to the French Grand Ouest. In the Haut Maine region, Le Mans is a city of art as well as a historic city, which played a decisive role in the development of the automobile. The country of Le Mans is distinguished by the diversity of its heritage, having kept in its stones the imprints of all eras. This region is notably renowned for its poulet de Loué, its capon and many other regional specialities. Let's go for a real Sarthe gourmet journey, with veal rouelles à la mancelle, roast poularde and seasonal fruit tart.

programme.title: Luana's Kitchen
programme.desc: With her friend Myriam, Luana Belmondo prepares two saffron-based recipes. On the program: orecchiette (small Italian pasta) with sausage, and monkfish with lemon confit and asparagus purée.

programme.title: Luana's Kitchen
programme.desc: In this episode, Luana welcomes Héloïse Brion, creator of "Miss Maggie's Kitchen," for a unique culinary journey in Normandy. Héloïse, who has French-American roots, offers a clever blend of her American heritage and her life in Normandy. Together, they cook two original recipes: a stuffed squash with apples, inspired by local traditions, and a pecan pie, emblematic of American cuisine.

programme.title: Earth from Above
programme.desc: Canada is the second largest country in the world by land mass and contains amazing natural resources: 7% of the Earth’s drinking water is spread over the country’s thousands of lakes. Forests cover 45% of the territory. Yann Arthus-Bertrand goes off to discover these resources with those whose job it is to protect them. He takes a look at the ecological balance sheet of the world’s eighth-largest economic power.

programme.title: Earth from Above
programme.sub-title: The sea needs us as we need the sea - Part 1
programme.desc: The oceans cover more than 70% of the Earth's surface. The sea is the largest natural environment on our planet and remains virtually unexploited. In Corsica, from a tower on Capo Rosso and in the Calanques de Piana. In the Galapagos, we have made a portrait of Paul Watson, ecologist and co-founder of Greenpeace. This Canadian with the physique of an adventurer has taken up the defence of marine animals. In Corsica, in the Bouches de Bonifacio, the Mediterranean basin is one of the richest in biodiversity on the planet. In Corsica, with overfishing. Worldwide, 75% of fish stocks are threatened by overfishing. The cause? Large-scale, wasteful and insufficiently regulated fishing. In Guinea-Bissau, the Bijagos, a string of a hundred or so islands, fish abound in these waters, but for how much longer? In Corsica, on the Sanguinaires Islands, almost 50% of the fish we eat comes from farming. In Norway, the sea is very fragile. There is a balance that has been established over millions of.

programme.title: Earth from Above
programme.sub-title: So the great rivers may live - Part 2
programme.desc: Yann Arthus-Bertrand thus continues his world tour and his inventory of the planet with the great rivers that suffer from man's excesses as a common thread. " So the great rivers may live" is the discovery of places, men and women who are fighting so that our waterways simply have their place on Earth. Thanks to his genius, man is correcting his mistakes: the Aral Sea, which once disappeared, is coming back. In New York, millions of people have drinking water thanks to the natural virtues of the forest.

programme.title: Earth from Above
programme.sub-title: The sea needs us as we need the sea - Part 2
programme.desc: The oceans cover more than 70% of the Earth's surface. The sea is the largest natural environment on our planet and remains virtually unexploited. In Brittany, in the Seven Islands. Then in the Bay of Saint-Brieuc, in the middle of a sea of green algae. In Brittany, intensive agriculture has developed over the last thirty years. In New Caledonia, the coral reef is the second largest in the world and could be threatened by the construction of a nickel mine. In Normandy, in the Botanical Garden of Vauville, an extraordinary garden has plants from all over the world. Also in the Archipelago of Chausey in Normandy with the highest tides in Europe. Or the Mont Saint Michel. As a result of silting up and man-made works, the Mont was no longer an island. In Italy, in Venice, on the verge of drowning, major development work, industrialisation and tourism have upset the environment. In New Caledonia, flying over the heart of Voh is surrounded by the largest lagoon in the world. 24,000 km2 prot.

programme.title: Earth from Above
programme.desc: The call of the Forest is about discovering places but above all it is about meeting those who protect this priceless heritage. Forests are essential to mankind. They capture CO2, promote the formation of clouds and therefore rain, protect the soil from erosion and provide a habitat for wildlife. From Madagascar, to France, to Cameroon, or even Eritrea, Yann Arthus-Bertrand sets out to discover the most beautiful forests, those who live in them, those who protect them and those who live off them.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: Honey was the first sweet condiment in history! It has also been known and consumed as a remedy since Antiquity. In France, we find an infinite variety of honey: acacia, chestnut, fir, rosemary, orange, spruce, oak, linden or lavender... We'll cross forests, fields and even towns, as bees also forage in urbanized areas. We'll then cook up emblematic recipes like Vercel gingerbread. Finally, we'll discover the European dark bee. Protecting this 80-million-year-old bee has become the spearhead of some passionate beekeepers.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: Auxerre is cut by valleys whose best exposed slopes are home to vineyards. The meandering course of the Yonne runs vertically through this region. To the east of Auxerre, the Chablis region is rounded with hills. The vineyard, extending on both sides of the valley of the Serein. To the south, lined by the Nivernais canal, the upper Yonne valley attracts climbing enthusiasts and boaters, before being swollen by the waters of the Cure. The region is renowned throughout the world for the quality of its wines, particularly those of Chablis. Julie begins her journey in Auxerre and then proposes typical recipes from the area: croquignoles and cherry clafoutis.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: Every year, the return of summer is a special moment, heralding the arrival of all those beautiful fruits on the shelves. Whether red, exotic or forgotten, fruit is an essential part of our diet. Today, we're off to discover summer fruits, which are harvested from June to August: peaches, melons, strawberries, raspberries... We'll head to Céret, the cherry capital, and then cook blueberries, strawberries and an apricot charlotte.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: This week, it is 80 kms from the capital, in Fontainebleau, that Julie is putting down her bags. Fontainebleau, a name famous throughout the world, a magical name which evokes for some a forest, for others a castle, a name which still shines with its royal history. The forest of Fontainebleau has inspired the art world since the beginning of the 19th century. Landscape painters such as Corot and Millet drew inspiration for their works there. But Fontainebleau has many other treasures in its bag, and gastronomy is part of its heritage. This is what Julie will discover through three recipes: Quail with grapes, raspberry and poppy pie and crayfish grave.

programme.title: Luana's Kitchen
programme.desc: Luana cooks with the interpreter of the flagship title of Frozen: Anaïs Delva. Together, they will prepare two 100% vegetarian recipes, a philosophy adopted by the singer. On the menu: grilled zucchini fettucini, white beans with pesto and a vegetarian burger. Proof that it's possible to enjoy vegetarian dishes without going hungry!

programme.title: Luana's Kitchen
programme.desc: In this episode, Luana Belmondo cooks a Mediterranean fish, red mullet. On the menu: red mullet fillets with avocado purée and carrots with cumin, and red mullet mille-feuille with spring vegetables.

programme.title: Earth from Above
programme.desc: With Bangladesh as a running thread, Yann Arthus-Bertrand meets several people who have changed their lives to dedicate themselves to a major project. In Bangladesh, Yves and Runa Marre have created the Friendship Foundation. Among other things, they’ve created a floating hospital installed on an old barge bought in France. Julie Andersen, an ex-advertising executive from New York has come to South Africa to defend sharks with her Shark Angels Foundation. In North India, Kartik Satyanarayan is helping to stop the dreadful exploitation of the lippus bears (dancing bears). He’s created Wildlife SOS, a preserve to rehabilitate the bears that have been rescued and to give work to the men of the tribe who were traditionally bear tamers and entertainers.

programme.title: Earth from Above
programme.desc: With Bangladesh as a running thread, Yann Arthus-Bertrand meets several people who have changed their lives to dedicate themselves to a major project. programme.title: Earth from Above
programme.desc: For this new episode, Yann Arthus-Bertrand travels through Senegal to encounter men and women who dedicate their lives to preserving the environment. One of the major ecological stakes of the country is fishing and the mangrove ecosystem which, like in some many other parts of the world, faces major threats. Yann Arthus-Bertrand presents the struggle of Haidar El Ali, chosen among one of the world’s most active ecologists. He creates protected marine areas and reforests the disappeared mangrove of his country. He’s managed to convince thousands of Senegalese to plant with him ten million mangrove trees.

programme.title: The Great Garden Challenge
programme.desc: It's final time as the competition reaches its climax with just two pairs of professional garden designers remaining. It’s a battle of the relative new kids on the block as Millie Souter and Max Parker-Smith take on Tamara Bridge and Kate Savill. Both pairs wowed the judges with their designs and planting in the previous round but now they take on their toughest challenge yet as they compete for the crown. They have to create show gardens at one of the World’s greatest gardens, RHS Wisley Gardens in Surrey, for a budget of £10,000. With a brief set by the gardens curator they’ll need to take their designs to the next level if their want to win, and they’ve only got 48 hours to complete them. Adding to the pressure the weather is also against them.

We'll then move on to Auvergne to discover how the famous Label Rouge is awarded and the role of certifying bodies ... because it's important to know what ends up on our plates. Julie also travels to the Drôme to cook guinea fowl, before heading to the Périgord to prepare a turkey stew. Julie will then head back up towards the center to discover an amazing fly maker who uses rooster feathers!

programme.title: Big Little Footprints
programme.desc: We travel to the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Canadian Rocky Mountains for their stunning natural beauty, historical castles, and epic adventures for the whole family. This is a destination where protecting its natural resources comes before anything else.

programme.title: Big Little Footprints
programme.desc: To educate our children about the profound impact of travel we travel to Miami, Florida. We'll learn about the area's colorful history, taste test its cuisine, learn Latin dancing and experience an epic adventure through the everglades - if we can make it out of alligator infested waters first!

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: Eating flowers might appear unconventional, but we often consume them without even realizing it. Consider artichokes, for instance : they are essentially large, unopened flowers. Capers are the preserved buds of flowers soaked in vinegar, and cloves are dried flower buds. We also find courgette flowers, saffron pistils, orange blossom water used to flavor pastries, and the violet sweets that evoke memories of our childhood. In addition to adding aesthetic appeal and providing a dose of vitamins to our plates, flowers elevate the flavors of a dish and can even serve as a vegetable substitute.

programme.title: Big Little Footprints
programme.sub-title: Eco-Explore Your Backyard - California Coast To Santa Barbara
programme.desc: In this episode we remind viewers just how much you can find when exploring your own backyard by road tripping the California Coast to Santa Barbara! Swapping TV time to chats around the campfire and an exciting encounter with sea lions.

programme.title: Big Little Footprints
programme.desc: If the Atlantis Bahamas isn’t on your family's bucket list - it should be! We’ll show you why as each family member ticks off their dream adventure that also gives back. Proving this big resort has an even bigger heart.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: Honey was the first sweet condiment in history! It has also been known and consumed as a remedy since Antiquity. In France, we find an infinite variety of honey: acacia, chestnut, fir, rosemary, orange, spruce, oak, linden or lavender... We'll cross forests, fields and even towns, as bees also forage in urbanized areas. We'll then cook up emblematic recipes like Vercel gingerbread. Finally, we'll discover the European dark bee. Protecting this 80-million-year-old bee has become the spearhead of some passionate beekeepers.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: We are in the middle of the harvest season, a perfect opportunity to discover the most beautiful French vineyards. Our trip starts with a bit of tourism. We will cross the Drôme with Tain l'Hermitage and its Baume de Venise, but also the Bordeaux region where the different domains compete to attract this new clientele. Then we head for Épernay, capital of the Champagne region, where the reputation of its sparkling wine is well established. Julie will take us to Burgundy, where the most expensive wines in the world are produced, and then back to Bordeaux, to immerse ourselves in the world of high-tech and biodynamic wines.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: Today, Julie takes us on a mushroom tour. There is nothing better to occupy your weekends than a walk in the forest in search of edible mushrooms. Some species, such as the cep or the chanterelle, can be preserved very well in the freezer or, for the more patient, in jars. We will also meet two chefs who are passionate about mushrooms and have become specialists in the subject: Franck Quinton and Régis Marcon. But for the moment, we're on the road, discovering typically French dishes with astonishing button mushrooms in Touraine, morels in the Jura, ceps in Gironde, russules charbonnières in Normandy and coulemelles in Auvergne!

programme.title: Luana's Kitchen
programme.desc: In this episode, Luana welcomes Héloïse Brion, creator of "Miss Maggie's Kitchen," for a unique culinary journey in Normandy. Héloïse, who has French-American roots, offers a clever blend of her American heritage and her life in Normandy. Together, they cook two original recipes: a stuffed squash with apples, inspired by local traditions, and a pecan pie, emblematic of American cuisine.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: Summer is the season when vegetables abound in the garden, but it would be a shame not to savor those that the cooler seasons have to offer: soups, pies, stews or gratins highlight seasonal vegetables, perfect for a nice warm up. To begin this new journey, Julie will cook salsify. This little tour of France will also allow us to meet gardening goldsmiths who sculpt winter vegetables and fruits. Finally, we will conclude as usual with a recipe from a chef, who will go out of his way to create a seasonal recipe for us.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: It is a mushroom that we are going to focus on today. A mushroom, or a black diamond, some would say: the truffle. And along the way, we will twist the neck of some clichés. Truffle hunting with dogs, with a sow but also flies... markets and of course cooking to discover or rediscover this mysterious mushroom, in all its aspects, in a salty but also sweet version... Richerenches, Carpentras, Saint Avère, Toulouse, Aix en Provence… the south of France will honor this black diamond!

programme.title: Earth from Above
programme.sub-title: So the great rivers may live - Part 2
programme.desc: Yann Arthus-Bertrand thus continues his world tour and his inventory of the planet with the great rivers that suffer from man's excesses as a common thread. " So the great rivers may live" is the discovery of places, men and women who are fighting so that our waterways simply have their place on Earth. Thanks to his genius, man is correcting his mistakes: the Aral Sea, which once disappeared, is coming back. In New York, millions of people have drinking water thanks to the natural virtues of the forest.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: Let's hit the roads of France to discover shellfish. We'll visit Brittany, then the Normandy coast where fishing is the regional sport, and Corsica, where the far northeast of the island lives to the rhythm of lobster. Julie takes us to cook lobster, crab with a very special recipe, and langoustines.

programme.title: Earth from Above
programme.desc: The call of the Forest is about discovering places but above all it is about meeting those who protect this priceless heritage. Forests are essential to mankind. They capture CO2, promote the formation of clouds and therefore rain, protect the soil from erosion and provide a habitat for wildlife. From Madagascar, to France, to Cameroon, or even Eritrea, Yann Arthus-Bertrand sets out to discover the most beautiful forests, those who live in them, those who protect them and those who live off them.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: It is in Giverny that Julie's journey begins, the place whose name resounds as the cradle of Impressionism has kept a moving authenticity. Its fame is strongly linked to the historical presence of Claude Monet and to all the fabulous witnesses left by him. Claude Monet also left his mark on the cooking in Giverny. His recipe books are there to testify to this. It’s with these notebooks that Julie will be inspired to fill hers, on the menu: Rabbit in compote, andouilles puff pastry with camembert, and apricot charlottes.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: Auxerre is cut by valleys whose best exposed slopes are home to vineyards. The meandering course of the Yonne runs vertically through this region. To the east of Auxerre, the Chablis region is rounded with hills. The vineyard, extending on both sides of the valley of the Serein. To the south, lined by the Nivernais canal, the upper Yonne valley attracts climbing enthusiasts and boaters, before being swollen by the waters of the Cure. The region is renowned throughout the world for the quality of its wines, particularly those of Chablis. Julie begins her journey in Auxerre and then proposes typical recipes from the area: croquignoles and cherry clafoutis.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: Head north to discover a French city that cannot be ignored: Lille. The city has an exceptional architectural heritage, a merchant town since the Middle Ages, a citadel under Louis XIV, an industrial town in the 19th century... it expanded over the centuries. Julie will meet those who contribute to the fame of the city and its region, through its culinary heritage with the menu of this journey: the recipe of the coq à la bière, that of the hochepot and for a sweet note, a crème brûlée with chicory. .

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook
programme.desc: This week, it is 80 kms from the capital, in Fontainebleau, that Julie is putting down her bags. Fontainebleau, a name famous throughout the world, a magical name which evokes for some a forest, for others a castle, a name which still shines with its royal history. The forest of Fontainebleau has inspired the art world since the beginning of the 19th century. Landscape painters such as Corot and Millet drew inspiration for their works there. But Fontainebleau has many other treasures in its bag, and gastronomy is part of its heritage. This is what Julie will discover through three recipes: Quail with grapes, raspberry and poppy pie and crayfish grave.

programme.title: Luana's Kitchen
programme.desc: In this episode, Luana Belmondo welcomes Delphine Malachard, who is gluten intolerant. Together, they cook gluten-free recipes. On the menu: chocolate soufflé and vanilla and red fruit financiers.

programme.title: Luana's Kitchen
programme.desc: Luana Belmondo cooks the queen of vegetable proteins: lentils. Healthy, easily digestible and delicious, it replaces meat and fish. We're going to prepare spiced coral lentil patties, with a yoghurt and mint sauce. Next up, a classic French dish: green lentil salad with Morteau sausage.

programme.title: Health Investigation
programme.sub-title: Aging at Home: the Best Choice?
programme.desc: Most French people want to live at home for as long as possible. It has even become a priority following the recent scandals that have rocked care homes. But to enable people to remain in their own homes for as long as possible, the right choices need to be made. Home adaptations, assistance with daily living, telecare… What are the keys to ageing well at home? Is it possible to avoid a care home right until the end? And how much does staying at home really cost?Care homes have never been anyone’s dream. But since the scandals that have rocked the Orpea group, more than ever, the French want to grow old at home. But what can you do when health problems pile up, when you lose your balance or can no longer cook for yourself? Staying at home quickly becomes impossible without outside help or home adaptations. Support is available – everyone knows that – but where should you turn to get it?To support our elderly people across France, an army of professionals travels thousands of kilometr.

programme.title: Health Investigation
programme.desc: In France, the menopause affects more than 11 million women, and every year a further 400,000 women experience it for the first time. Occurring at an average age of 51, the menopause marks the start of a new phase of life – a period that is becoming longer as life expectancy increases. Yet it remains a taboo subject about which very little is known. Hot flushes, sleep and mood disturbances, weight gain, reduced libido… The drop in hormone levels can trigger symptoms that vary greatly from one woman to another. Some women experience none at all, whilst others experience many. And whilst the menopause is not an illness, it can increase the risk of serious conditions such as osteoporosis or cardiovascular events. Screening for risk factors is therefore a public health priority. Yet France lags far behind in the management of the menopause.Once touted as a panacea, hormone replacement therapy (HRT) has been at the centre of a major controversy for the past twenty years or so, accused of.

programme.title: Health Investigation
programme.desc: With 8 million dogs and 14 million cats, the French hold the world record for pet ownership. Whilst these four-legged companions soothe and stimulate us, they actually do much more than that: they heal us! And this has been scientifically proven. Having a pet at home has numerous benefits for our physical and mental well-being.Better cardiovascular health, a stronger immune system and gut microbiota, and the release of oxytocin – the ‘happiness hormone’… There are countless studies demonstrating the physical, psychological and emotional benefits of this bond between humans and animals.For the past forty years or so, animal-assisted therapy has been growing in popularity in France. Dogs, cats, horses and certain farm animals now work alongside therapists to offer a new approach to care. In care homes, dogs help to rekindle the desire to communicate in elderly people suffering from Alzheimer’s disease. For children with psychomotor disabilities, horses facilitate functional rehabilitat.

programme.title: Baby Animals Down Under
programme.desc: Bli med inn i Australias skoger og møt noen av de fascinerende dyreungene som vokser opp her. Følg koalaungene fra den første trygge tiden i moras pung til de begynner å klatre og utforske omgivelsene. Se når flygehundungene lærer å fly, mens kokaburraungene finner stemmen sin og våger seg ut av reiret. I regnskogene i Queensland titter sjeldne trekenguruunger fram fra moras pung, mens stripete kasuarkyllinger lærer det de trenger for å overleve av sin omsorgsfulle far. Vi møter også pungrotter, og til og med små larver, som vokser og utvikler seg og forbereder seg på livet på egen hånd. Gjennom fascinerende dyreatferd og nære familiehistorier får vi oppleve utfordringene, overraskelsene og de avgjørende stegene på veien mot et selvstendig liv for de yngste beboerne i Australias skoger.

programme.title: Panda School
programme.desc: De små pandaungene lærer at det er vanskeligere å spise bambusblad enn å spise skudd, og de blir fortrolige med å klatre i regnvær. Wolongs toppmoderne fødeklinikk må ta seg av friske nyfødte, mens pandaene som skal settes ut i naturen lenger oppe i fjellet må venne seg til snøen. Et par ambassadørpandaer forbereder seg på et nytt liv i utlandet.

programme.title: Panda School
programme.desc: En ny klasse starter på Pandaskolen. De små pandaungene har tilbrakt hele livet på fødeavdelingen, men skal nå for første gang våge seg ut i en verden full av nye inntrykk, nye lyder og pandaferdigheter de må lære. Mini Ling Lang, den eldste av sommerungene, oppdager at mora hennes er en flink klatrer og prøver å følge i hennes fotspor. Su Jin Junior er egenrådig, og mora hans holder han i sjakk med en streng og direkte undervisningsstil. De små tvillingene er for unge til å begynne å klatre, men gir alt når snøen kommer. Snøvær betyr ikke at skolen er avlyst, det betyr at timene blir vanskeligere. Mens de minste ungene begynner på skolen, er Tian Tians unge oppe i fjellene og nærmer seg slutten av undervisningen…og kommer litt nærmere et liv i naturen.

programme.title: Redd sjiraffene: Den lange hjemreisen
programme.desc: En kraftig flom fanger åtte sjeldne sjiraffer på en øy. Om de ikke får hjelp, kan de dø. Men løsningen er komplisert: å bygge en moderne ark, få sjiraffene til å gå om bord og seile dem i land før de sulter. Klokka går. Kan teamet med kenyanske veterinærer, stammeledere og miljøvernere fra hele verden lykkes med oppdraget?

programme.title: Baby Animals Down Under
programme.desc: Langt fra Australias storbyer og kystområder strekker den enorme villmarken seg utover, et barskt landskap der dyreungene raskt må lære å overleve. Vi møter en rekke fascinerende dyreunger som tar sine første skritt mot selvstendighet, fra emuunger som blir tatt hånd om av omsorgsfulle fedre, til dingovalper som lærer flokkens regler, og kamelkalver som krysser ørkenen sammen med sine beskyttende mødre. Unge røde kjempekenguruer prøver ut de kraftige beina som skal bære dem gjennom livet, mens undulatunger gjør seg klare til sine første flyturer over de røde slettene. Andre steder kommer nyklekte skjeggagamer og innlandstaipaner til verden, klare til å overleve på egen hånd. Gjennom sine første måltider, viktige lærdommer fra familien, lange vandringer og avgjørende milepæler på veien mot voksenlivet, lærer disse hardføre dyreungene å mestre tilværelsen i et av jordas mest ugjestmilde miljø.

programme.desc: National Geographics filmskaper Bertie Gregory legger ut på en eventyrlig reise til den legendariske øygruppen Sør-Georgia.

programme.desc: National Geographic blir med på en spennende reise over 445 kilometer for å utforske Grand Canyon og dens mysterier.

programme.title: Australia's Wild Woodlands
programme.desc: Australias vidstrakte eukalyptusskoger huser et utrolig utvalg av arter som ikke finnes andre stedet i verden. Mange av disse eldgamle økosystemene har i stor grad forblitt uendret helt siden dinosaurenes tid, men nå er fremtiden usikker for flere arter. Vi avdekker hvordan klimaendringene endrer den sarte balansen for disse utrolige dyrene som lever i disse majestetiske skogene.

programme.title: Utemmede Filippinene
programme.desc: Vi begynner på den lille øya Batan, der vi treffer en unik slange og en utbredt landkrabbe.

programme.title: Croc Wars: Grumeti Vs Mara
programme.desc: Hvert år krysser nesten to millioner gnuer og sebraer Serengetis to elver, Grumeti og Mara. Her venter dynastier av nilkrokodiller på sitt årlige etegilde. Men i krokodillenes verden er ikke alle drapsstrategier de samme. Fra brutale bakholdsangrep til frekke tyverier – disse smarte rovdyrene benytter seg av helt ulike taktikker under den viktige jakten på ett måltid i to elver.

programme.sub-title: Mysterious North: Land of Mountain Forests
programme.desc: Fra pangoliner, asiatiske palmesivetter og Delacours langurer til cat ba-langurer og de nylig oppdagede vitenamesiske krokodilleøglene. Vi ser på det utrolige utvalget av unike dyr som trives i de ekstreme forholdene som finnes i de skogkledde fjellene i Vietnam.

programme.title: Wild Vietnam
programme.desc: Fra gibbonaper, makaker, grønne havskilpadder og orientalske kloløse dvergotere til kragebjørner, siamkrokodiller og asiagapenebb. Vi møter de bemerkelsesverdige dyrene som har tilpasset seg et liv i de unikt tøffe forholdene og ekstreme klimaene i det sørlige Vietnams tropiske habitater.

programme.title: Race to Winter
programme.desc: Når vårens første lys glir over fjordene, skogene, fjellene og tundraen, starter den store oppvåkningen. Brunbjørnmødrene kommer ut av vinterdvalen, og leder ungene sine ut i en helt ny verden. Lundefuglene gjenforenes med sine livspartnere, og isbjørnene vandrer rundt på den smeltende isen. Men de har lite tid - skyggen av vinteren lurer. Og I dette uendelige løpet mot kulden er det kun de mest motstandsdyktige som klarer seg.

programme.title: Vill vinter
programme.desc: Å overleve i skogene nord i Finland er et kappløp mot årstidene, med sin grove villmark og ekstreme klima. Vi følger det utrolige dagliglivet til en brunbjørnmor som risikerer alt for å oppdra ungene sine. Hun kommer ut av vinterdvalen tynn og sliten, og må lede ungene gjennom en kort sommer der mat – og overlevelse – er det eneste på prioriteringslisten.

programme.title: The Incredible Honey Badger
programme.desc: Fra fødselen av må honninggrevlingen klare seg gjennom skorpionstikk og angrep fra bier, og bygger opp en overnaturlig motstand mot gift og smerte. Når de blir større, tar disse fryktløse dyrene opp kampen mot rovdyr som er mye større – løver, leoparder og andre – og stoler på sine skjerpede sanser, løse hud og ukuelige kampånd. Fantastiske opptak av ekte konfrontasjoner viser hvordan de tøffe og motstandsdyktige honninggrevlingene er nesten uovervinnelige.

programme.desc: Det er vår i Michigan, og det betyr dyreunger på gårdene. Reinsdyrkalver og geitekillinger er noen av dyrene som skaper trengsel på klinikken. Et piggete kjæledyr, en kylling med parasitter og en betennelse i bukspyttkjertelen gir veterinærene mye å gjøre i dagens episode av "Den fantastiske dr. Pol".

programme.title: Den fantastiske dr. Pol
programme.desc: I ukas "Den fantastiske dr. Pol" ser veterinærene til en rekke dyreunger, blant annet et kull med kattunger og en geitekilling. Men alt er ikke fryd og gammen, for dr. Nicole får en blodig oppgave på en gård i Michigan, dr. Brenda undersøker et reinsdyr som ikke kan gå og dr. Pol behandler en katt som var døden nær. Dyreungene og gårdsutrykningene gjør det til en travel uke for Pols veterinærklinikk.
